key_insight: ActMOF turns real microwave MOF synthesis data into a benchmark that shows Gaussian-process active learning is especially effective in sparse crystallization search spaces.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps materials engineers choose and compare optimization strategies before running costly experiments, improving the odds of rapid crystalline MOF discovery.
method: Encoded experimentally measured microwave synthesis conditions with a crystallinity index from diffraction peak intensity and FWHM.
Benchmarked search policies using Gaussian processes, tree ensembles, and large language models.
Transferred the best-guided search to six related aluminum-MOF syntheses under a fixed experimental budget.
evidence_signal: The study used experimentally grounded data and reported that all six follow-up synthesis campaigns produced crystalline products within 12 experiments each.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the underlying experimental data, so results may not transfer unchanged to other MOF families or synthesis platforms.
paper_title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
